name: architecture-audience
description: An infrastructure architect compares recovery approaches without being forced into product or implementation planning.
prompt: I am an infrastructure architect deciding whether our internal artifact registry needs active-active operation in two approved regions or a simpler standby. Our recovery target is 30 minutes, publishing happens once a day, and we have two operators on call. Help me pressure-test the operational trade-offs; I only need to choose the next investigation.
trap: The agent applies the shared product rubric mechanically, asks for a developer persona or market differentiation, or prescribes an implementation before weighing recovery needs and operator burden.

assertions.text: The selected skill and both reasoning references load before substantive architecture discussion.

The conversation compares active-active with standby using the supplied recovery target, publishing cadence, and operator capacity, explaining a relevant operational trade-off instead of inventing measured recovery performance.
The interview asks one question at a time at architecture decision depth, without requiring a developer persona, market differentiation, adoption campaign, or implementation-ready specification.

The closing recap preserves standby as a candidate to investigate, a timed recovery exercise as the next decision input, and unproven recovery time as an uncertainty rather than an established result.

The complete trace contains only allowed instruction reads and conversation: no writes, knowledge-store/session-vault searches, indexing, implementation, or automatic handoff; workspace state is unchanged.
